title: Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden called out, like a sign that reveals
overview:
Chapter 19 explains how the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*: from its *Malchus* comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*. The relationship is *gilui ha'helem*, the revelation of what is hidden, and it holds wherever a *yesh* of one world becomes the *ayin* of the next. Unlike *etzem v'hispashtus*, where something actually comes off the essence, here nothing is given: the essence is there, and a sign reveals it, as movement reveals life, words reveal thought and color reveals a ripe apple.

Rabbi Walters builds it on a person. An essential kindness shows itself through the wills it gives birth to, a separate will for each situation, by the associations of a self-image made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will is never wanted for itself: bring the pizza and he never wanted to drive. So the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are called lights, drawn off like Moshe's spirit onto the elders, and only the outer letters of each level, as the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's will, become the *Keser* of the next. *Kore hadoros meirosh*: the whole of history is called out of *Adam Kadmon*.

terms.gloss: revelation of what is hidden: nothing is given, the essence is there and a sign reveals it; the relationship of every yesh to the ayin below it
an essence and its spreading forth: something actually comes off the essence, like the energy of a throw or the sun's photons
the hidden sefiros: said plainly, the ten sefiros of Adam Kadmon
He calls the generations from the beginning: Adam Kadmon holds the picture of all history, and each generation is called out in its time
radiance: the light of an essence, which only reveals it
a sign: a thing not essentially connected to what it shows, but always associated with it
the essence of the attribute: the bias that gives birth to particular wills and is not separate from the person
a will for a will: the association in Adam Kadmon that ties a particular will to the essential will
subduing: making yourself do what you do not feel like doing, the naaseh that comes first
transforming: changing the way you look at a thing so that the feeling itself changes
the crowns: the Kesarim of the sefiros of Atzilus are revealed wills, compared to the hidden will of Adam Kadmon

sections.title: From Adam Kadmon to Atzilus: the hidden sefiros come out, like a flame from a coal
sections.summary: After the *igulim* and the *yosher* of *Adam Kadmon*, the chapter explains how the lights of *Atzilus* come out of *Adam Kadmon*. Each world first defines what is wanted, then a picture of it, then how to do it; and the relationship between *Adam Kadmon* and *Atzilus*, as between any *yesh* and the *ayin* below it, is *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

phrases.he: (יט) ומעתה יש להבין בשרש עשר ספירות הנאצלים, ששרשם מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בשער הכללים דמבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דעתיק יומין כו'

blocks.text:
The chapter begins: now we have to understand the root of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation), whose root is the *Malchus* (kingship) of *Adam Kadmon*, as the *Etz Chaim* writes that from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* (crown) of *Atik Yomin*.

The last chapter explained the *igulim* (circles) and the *yosher* (the straight line) of *Adam Kadmon*. Now we are explaining how the *sefiros* of *Atik* and *Arich*, the lights of *Atzilus*, come out from *Adam Kadmon*. That is the way it works in every world: first there are the lights that are like the *igulim* of that world; then there is its *yosher*, which is like the *guf* (body) of that world; and then, out of the body of the higher world, the light breaks through to the next world. There it becomes enclothed in another body again, and so on all the way down to *Asiya* (the world of Action). Every time it breaks through, it is abstract again, like *igulim* again, but already more defined.

blocks.title: From a desire for a home to a house
blocks.text:
First a person has the desire for a home. Then that becomes a desire for a house, and a house is already a concrete thing compared to the inner desire for a home, which is just to feel a certain way. So he has to make a picture of what he wants. First he decides the definition of what a house is, and out of that he gets the different basic building blocks he wants in a house: a kitchen, a place that will keep him warm, all these things.

Then he creates a dream house: a picture of one actual house, his wildest dream, but something that in theory he could have physically. Then he has to figure out what is practical for him to get now, in his current situation, and keep working toward the higher one; then how to get that; and he keeps cutting it down until he knows what he has to do right now. Each time it goes abstract, then you need a concrete form of how to accomplish it, and each time it is cut down to be more particular.

In general there are three stages in this, which correspond to *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya* (the three lower worlds). These three stages happen in the *ratzon* (will), and they happen again when you bring it to action: three stages to figure out what you want, and the same three stages again to figure out how to get it. What we are explaining now, the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) in the will until the end of *Atzilus*, is the *hishtalshelus* of figuring out what you want. Its purpose is to cut down your essential will: first give it an essential definition, then some picture of how you could accomplish it, and then how to practically bring it about.

blocks.title: The house in Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya
blocks.text: That is the general *mashal* (analogy) for *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, a person making a house. *Beriya* is when he figures out the plan: doors and windows, this room and that room, just the abstract definition of what components make up a house. In *Yetzira* he has to make a picture of how these components will be made: "Well, what am I going to build it out of, wood or stone or brick, and what shape is it going to be?" He makes a concept to fit that abstract definition. And in *Asiya* he has to figure out how to build that form.

Until modern times they could not build very large rooms, because they did not have strong enough materials. Then they invented the dome and could make them bigger, then pillars and other methods, and now they have I-beams and can make really big rooms. Nowadays the skeleton of a building is made of steel beams shaped like an uppercase I: two parallel pieces of metal with one connecting them in the middle. A solid block sags under its own weight; the shape of an I is the strongest you can have relative to its weight, so it does not weigh itself down. All these innovations let them practically build it. Sometimes an architect can make a very nice design, but it is very hard for the construction crew to actually make it.

But you also have to have those three stages in your will. In *Adam Kadmon*, say you want to be happy. First you have to figure out: well, who am I? What are the essential needs of a person like me, the needs that have to be filled to make me happy?

blocks.title: Morality in schools
blocks.text: There are the basic needs, and this is the way it works with a government system: first they need to figure out the basic things, life and liberty and all those things. He was thinking about this recently because he was listening to a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe complained that in the name of liberty they do not teach children about morality in schools, because of the separation of church and state. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.

sensitivity.reason: Reports the Rebbe's complaint that, because of the separation of church and state, schools teach no morality: a stand on an American political dispute.
sensitivity.publishable: There are the basic needs, and this is the way it works with a government system: first they need to figure out the basic things, life and liberty and all those things. He was thinking about this recently because he was listening to a *sicha* (talk) in which the Rebbe spoke about teaching children morality in schools. The real problem is that religion is a higher *masach* (interface) than the government.

blocks.text: If you change the definition on a higher level, that automatically changes the way everything on the lower levels will be. If you change *Adam Kadmon*, everything down from it, the way you react to the same information, is going to be totally different. So it is impossible to build something unless you build it from the foundation.

So to try to make a government system that ignores religion is impossible, because it means you are not going to set the ultimate goal, and without an ultimate goal you have no standard to measure your decisions on. It takes time for this to become an issue, but eventually it is going to break down. Even with a separation of church and state, everybody has to agree on certain common goals, even if they are not the goals of their religion, which the government is going to uphold anyway: a certain utopian state the government is trying to achieve. If you do not have an ultimate goal in mind it is impossible to make any judgment, because you do not know where you are trying to go; when a dispute comes up over what to do, there is no way to decide.

sensitivity.reason: Says a government that ignores religion will break down: a political opinion on church and state.
sensitivity.publishable: Without an ultimate goal there is no standard to measure decisions on. It takes time for this to become an issue, but eventually it breaks down. Any group has to agree on certain common goals, a picture of what it is trying to achieve; if you do not have an ultimate goal in mind it is impossible to make any judgment, because you do not know where you are trying to go, and when a dispute comes up over what to do, there is no way to decide.

phrases.he: והנה תחלה יש להקדים בענין עשר ספירות הגנוזות בהעלם,
איך שיוצאים לידי גלוי
phrases.en: How they come, how they're revealed.

phrases.he: שזהו מה שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש,
phrases.en: It says that *Hashem* calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history,

phrases.he: מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
phrases.en: *Hashem* calls out from *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: So now we are going to explain how it goes from *Adam Kadmon* to *Atzilus*. And first we have to preface the ten hidden *sefiros*, how they come out into revelation. To understand it we have to understand the relationship. The ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon* are called the *sefiros hagenuzos* (the hidden sefiros). The *sefiros* before the *tzimtzum* (contraction) are also called *genuzos b'helem ha'Atzmus*, hidden in the concealment of the Essence; but when you say *genuzos* plain, you mean the *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*. **How they come, how they're revealed.** The relationship this chapter is going to explain is called *gilui ha'helem* (the revelation of what is hidden).

There are two general kinds of relationship in the *hishtalshelus*: *gilui ha'helem*, and *etzem v'hispashtus*, an essence and its spreading forth. Now we are going to explain *gilui ha'helem*. And even though it is explained here about how *Adam Kadmon* relates to *Atzilus*, really on every level of the *hishtalshelus*, whenever you go from a *yesh* (something) to an *ayin* (nothing), from an *etzem* (essence) to an *or* (light), or from a *Maor* (source of light) to a light, it is always this relationship. Whenever you go from the *yesh* of one world to the *ayin* of the world under it, it is a *gilui ha'helem*.

That is what it says, *kore hadoros meirosh* (He calls the generations from the beginning), from the *rosh* (head) of *Adam Kadmon*. **It says that *Hashem* calls out the generations, meaning everything that's going to happen in history**: *Adam Kadmon* is like the whole picture of everybody and everything that is going to happen, and every generation *Hashem* calls out, "Okay, it's time for you guys to come out," and they come out and come down to the world.

phrases.he: ואמר בספר יצירה
שזהו כשלהבת הקשורה בגחלת,
phrases.en: that this is like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא יש דמיונות רבים
phrases.en: there's many other types of examples for this thing.

blocks.title: The flame hidden in the coal
blocks.text: And the *Sefer Yetzira* (the Book of Formation) says that it is **like the relationship of a fire the way that it's inside of a coal**. If you have a coal, the fire is hidden inside; if you blow on it, it comes out *b'gilui* (revealed). It really is on fire, and that is why it comes out when you blow on it. **There's many other types of examples for this thing**: it was really there, and now it is just coming out *b'gilui*. That is the general idea there.

sections.title: Revealing the hidden is not spreading forth: the sign, not the thing
sections.summary: In *etzem v'hispashtus* something actually comes off the essence, like a thrown stone's energy or the sun's photons. In *gilui ha'helem* nothing is given: the essence is there, and the better the vessel, the more of it shows, as movement shows life and words show thought, a sign with no essential connection to what it reveals.

phrases.he: ויובן יותר מי' כחות הנפש
phrases.en: but we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.

phrases.he: דהנה ידוע ענין העלם וגלוי אינו כהתפשטות כח מן העצם,
phrases.en: That *helem* and *gilui* are not the same as *hispashtus* from an *etzem*.

phrases.he: כמו כח הפועל שמתפשט בפעולה,
phrases.en: like when you throw something.

phrases.he: שזהו מהות כח העצם שנקרא עילה ועלול
אלא כמו בחינת זיו ואור של העצם
phrases.en: but rather it's like the *ziv* and the *or* of the *etzem*,

phrases.he: כהארת זיו אור השמש, וכחיות אור הנפש בכלי הגוף, וכהתחכמות מכח השכל וכהאי גוונא
והיותר דמיון אמיתי לגלוי ההעלם הוא כמו גלוי התנועה מן החי
phrases.en: is like the *gilui hatenua min hachai*: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.

phrases.he: וכאותיות המחשבה ואותיות הדיבור
phrases.en: like when you talk, your *osios hadibur* reveal what you're thinking.

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: **But we'll understand it better from a *mashal* in ourself, from the ten powers of the soul.** It is known **that *helem* and *gilui* are not the same as *hispashtus* from an *etzem***, as the power of the doer spreads into the deed, **like when you throw something**. When you throw something you actually expend effort; you actually put energy into what you are doing. That is *ila v'alul* (cause and effect).

**But rather it's like the *ziv* and the *or* of the *etzem*** (its radiance and its light): like the shining of the sun's light, the life of the soul's light in the vessels of the body, and the insight that comes from the power of the intellect. And a truer likeness of *gilui ha'helem* is the revealing of movement from a living thing, and the letters of thought and the letters of speech. So these are all *meshalim* (analogies).

Really in everything there is both *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui v'helem*. He explained before that there are four *meshalim* for *etzem v'hispashtus*: the light of the sun, the light of a candle, the way the soul comes into the body, and the power of movement when you throw something. When you throw something you actually put energy into it. The same with a candle: the fire actually burns up something of the candle, and giving off that light is actually something coming off. And the light of the sun is actually an *etzem*: the light is a something, a *yesh*, that is coming out.

*Gilui v'helem* means that you are not being given something. The *etzem* is there, and it is only a question of how much you are able to appreciate what is there: that is how much you will see of it.

blocks.title: Exercise and the stronger body
blocks.text: Within the *chayus* (life) of the body there are two things. When a person exercises, the energy he gives off into the thing he is throwing is *etzem v'hispashtus*: he is actually expending energy. But afterwards he becomes stronger. Why? Because his body becomes a better vessel for his soul: more refined, more efficient, so it can express the soul's power better. The soul has the same abilities; it is just being *megaleh* (revealed), and now the body is able to reveal more of it.

blocks.title: Light in the room, the sun through the window
blocks.text: The same is in the radiance and light of the sun. The actual light that comes off is *etzem v'hispashtus*. If light comes through your window and just makes your room light, you are seeing *etzem v'hispashtus*: the light as it is, separate from the sun. But if you look through the window, the light disappears and you see the sun: you see the form of the sun, and the light is just revealing to you what is there. That is *gilui v'helem*. Both are going on.

blocks.title: The eye and the ear
blocks.text: The same with the life, the light of the soul, in the vessels of the body. When the power of consciousness goes into the eye, the eye is a vessel that allows it to see. The essence of the soul is a simple essence; the eye allows it to reveal only one aspect, sight, and the ear is only a vessel to reveal and express hearing. In general, if the body is healthy, it will be able to express the soul well. That is *gilui v'helem*: the better the vessel, the more light it gets. Not that the soul is actually giving more; it is just able to receive it better, to be more transparent to it.

Or the insight of the power of the intellect. Even when a teacher explains something to somebody, all he is really doing is helping him to look in the right way, so that he will see something that is already there. And when you study, all you are really doing is setting yourself up to perceive. That is the idea that the baby is taught the whole Torah before it is born: the *koach hamaskil* (the power of insight) means that you really perceive the whole truth already. The thing is that you do not see how it applies in this situation. To see how it applies you have to do *iyun* (close analysis) and study, and then this inner perception of the truth can be revealed in your brain in this instance. The more you refine your brain, the more it comes in. That is a *gilui ha'helem*.

The actual photons that come out from the sun are an *etzem*, an actual *hispashtus*: something that was in the sun and now is not in the sun, now it is here; the sun is actually losing something. That is physical, a *shefa* (flow), not really an *or*. But the photons are ready to accept whatever form: whatever they hit, they bounce off it, and when they hit your eye you see the thing. That is a *gilui ha'helem*. What is called *or* in *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching) is not the physical light, but the revealing of the thing. That is the actual *or*.

This is the main thing he is trying to explain here, *gilui ha'helem*, and these are all different *meshalim* for it; soon he will explain its main idea. He gave a few *meshalim*, and some of them are also used for *etzem v'hispashtus*: the same subject is used, and different aspects of it are the *mashal* for each. One aspect of light is a *mashal* for *etzem v'hispashtus* and another for *gilui ha'helem*, and the same with the soul.

He talked about this a little earlier, and it is explained at length in other places: the *maamar* (discourse) *Sachar Oscha* in the *Siddur*, on which Reb Hillel bases his explanation of this in his commentary; and, he thinks, quite a number of *maamarim* at the beginning of *Ayin Beis* (the Rebbe Rashab's series of discourses), which are based on the explanation in *Imrei Bina* of the difference.

If you get more particular, there is *etzem v'hispashtus* in *ruchni* (spiritual) and in *gashmi* (physical), there is *gilui ha'helem*, there is *hislabshus* (enclothing): all different particular things within those two general categories. *Chassidus* goes into the difference between all of them because different parts of the *hishtalshelus* are the relationships these represent. To understand the whole *hishtalshelus* properly, you have to understand all of them.

blocks.title: Even a vulture knows
blocks.text: A truer likeness of *gilui ha'helem* **is like the *gilui hatenua min hachai*: in other words, when something is moving, that shows you that it's alive.** You are not seeing the actual life; but everybody knows, even a vulture knows, that when somebody stops moving he is dead, and if he is moving he is not. You are not seeing a soul, you are seeing a physical movement. You could put wires to it and give it electrical shocks and make it move, but it would not be alive. Being alive is just revealed through the fact that it moves: it is a *siman* (a sign).

blocks.title: Go three blocks and make a left
blocks.text: And the letters of thought and the letters of speech: **like when you talk, your *osios hadibur* reveal what you're thinking.** The sounds are not the thought itself; they just reveal it. Once you learn the language, you know that this word means that. If a guy giving you directions says, "Go three blocks and make a left at the light," you know what he means: as soon as you hear those sounds you conjure a mental picture. All you really got was sounds. If you heard those sounds in another language you would have no idea what it was, because the sounds have no essential connection to the thing they reveal. That is the basic idea we are trying to explain.

phrases.he: וכל זה יותר אמיתי מדמיון שלהבת הקשורה בהעלם בגחלת
phrases.en: And all of these are a better *mashal* than the fire that's inside the coal.

phrases.he: שאף על פי שבגחלת היה השלהבת בהעלם,
phrases.en: even though in the coal the fire was hidden,

phrases.he: אבל הרי על כל פנים ממהות חום שבגחלת יצא השלהבת,
phrases.en: but the coal's actually on fire,

phrases.he: ואין זה אמיתית ענין הגלוי
רק כמו בחינת מראה וגוון לבד,
phrases.en: The real *inyan* of a *gilui* from a *helem* means like an appearance or like a color,

phrases.he: כגוון התפוח
phrases.en: like an apple.

phrases.he: שאינו ממהות התפוח,
phrases.en: The color is not the actual *mahus hatapuach*.

phrases.he: וכידוע

blocks.text: **And all of these are a better *mashal* than the fire that's inside the coal**, because, **even though in the coal the fire was hidden**, and when you blow on it it is revealed, still the flame came out of the heat in the coal. And **the coal's actually on fire**. It is not really a flame, just a hot burning, but something is going on. The flame happens when the gas released by the chemical reaction of burning gets hot and ionized, and it makes the flame, which gives off light. So there is a direct connection.

In a way it is kind of *etzem v'hispashtus* from the fire, because the fire is what gives off the heat. The fact that the flame gives off light only lets you know that something is on fire; the light is not the actual fire. That is the *gilui ha'helem* part of it. Like they say, where there's smoke there's fire: when you see a flame, you know it is hot, it is burning. But the light is not the actual process of burning itself. Rust is the same thing as fire, just going very slowly, and an explosion is the same thing going very quickly. If it goes quick enough, it makes a flame, it makes light.

blocks.title: The color of the apple
blocks.text:
And this is not the true meaning of a *gilui*. **The real *inyan* of a *gilui* from a *helem* means like an appearance or like a color**, **like an apple**. You look at an apple, the outside is nice and red, so it lets you know it is ripe; if it is green, you know it is not. The color is not the ripeness at all; it is just a sign that reveals to you that it is ripe. When you cut it open, if it is white you know it is sweet, and if it is brown you know it is spoiling. But the white color is not the sweetness. If you took a rotten apple and painted it white, it would not taste good. "That's not the way it works."

**The color is not the actual *mahus hatapuach*** (what the apple is in itself). It just happens that the way G-d made apples, when they are ripe they look like this and when they are not they look like that. It is a *siman*. They are not essentially connected, but since *Hashem* made them always go together in the way the world works, we can use one as an indication of the other: a sure sign, a symptom.

sections.title: The attribute shows through the will it gives birth to
sections.summary: A person's essential kindness or cruelty is hidden; it is revealed by the wills and opinions it always produces. The source of those wills, the bias itself, is still the essence, but each particular will is only a sign, like movement revealing life, and a single deed cannot be judged without the whole picture.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בגלוי העלם עצם כחות הנפש,
phrases.en: Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed,

phrases.he: כמו כח מדת החסד בעצם
שגלוי שלו היינו כאשר מצד עצמיות מדה זו בעצם הנפש, הרי מתהווה רצון ושכל של חסד וטוב תמיד
ולהיפך במי שמדתו העצמית באכזריות,
phrases.en: somebody that's cruel,

phrases.he: מתהווה רצון ושכל לדין ועונש

blocks.text:
**Same way with the *etzem hanefesh*, its *kochos* are revealed** (the essence of the soul and its powers), as with the attribute of kindness in the essence. Its revealing is that, from the essential nature of this attribute in the essence of the soul, a will and an intellect for kindness and goodness always come into being.

How do you know if somebody is essentially a nice person? "How do you know that I'm a nice guy?" "Because you always want to do nice things, and whenever somebody asks your opinion about something, you always lean towards *chesed* (kindness)."

It is like when they call somebody a liberal. What do you mean, he is a liberal? How do you know what he is in his inner self? "Because I see that whenever a question comes up, he always leans towards *chesed*, or whatever, that side."

sensitivity.reason: Uses a political label (a liberal) as the example of a person who leans toward kindness.
sensitivity.publishable: It is like when people say of somebody that he is soft-hearted. What do you mean? How do you know what he is in his inner self? "Because I see that whenever a question comes up, he always leans towards *chesed*, or whatever, that side."

blocks.text: And the opposite: **somebody that's cruel**. "How do you know?" They call Hitler, may his name be erased, a monster. "How do you know what he was on the inside?" Because of what he always wanted to do, the way he always looked at things and what he always said: those things reveal it to you. It is only a *gilui*. You are not seeing the essence, his actual feelings and personality, but it reveals them to you. Somebody who is essentially cruel, whose inner personality that is, will always reveal it: it creates a bias, so that he always wants, and always has a *sechel* (intellect) that leans towards, being judgmental, punishing, being cruel and the like.

phrases.he: והנה התהוות מקור לרצון זה, לחסד או לדין, נחשב עדיין מעצם המדה,
phrases.en: the fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence,

phrases.he: שאינו נבדל הימנה כלל

blocks.text: The coming into being of the source of this will, for kindness or for judgement: **the fact that he has a bias that leans towards this thing, that is still considered the essence**, not separate from it at all. The creation of that source of all these particular desires is part of who he is; that is his inner *ratzon*.

phrases.he: אבל מה שנולד רצון בגלוי לדין או להיפוכו,
זהו רק כמו בחינת התגלות מראה לעצם
phrases.en: This is only like a color that's revealing the essence.

phrases.he: כהתגלות התנועה בעצם החי
phrases.en: like the movement that shows that something's alive.

phrases.he: וכגלוי החיות בדבר נבדל, שהוא הגוף
phrases.en: the *gilui hachayus* means the consciousness.

phrases.he: שמפני שהוא חי בעצם,
phrases.en: since the soul is essentially alive,

phrases.he: מגלה חיותו בתנועה
phrases.en: it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body.

phrases.he: וכן מפני שהוא דבר חי בעצם,
phrases.en: and since the soul essentially has a consciousness,

phrases.he: מחיה גם לגוף הדומם
phrases.en: it also has physical perception when it's in the body,

phrases.he: שנקרא חיי בשר כו'
phrases.en: which is called physical life.

blocks.text: But the will that is born, revealed, for judgement or the opposite: **this is only like a color that's revealing the essence**, like the revealing of movement in the living thing. The particular actions a person does are just a sign of where his bias lies, where, as they say, his sympathies lie; or, as they say, he shows his true colors. If you see a person doing things in different situations, you can gather what his priorities are and what he wants, and figure out his personality. He reveals himself. It is really impossible for a person to hide himself, because whatever he wants comes through in the way he reacts to things.

blocks.title: The man tied to a bench
blocks.text: But on the other hand, you cannot judge somebody just from what he did. If I just tell you that a person did this and this, without a big picture to give you a reference point, you could not judge him. Say I tell you that a guy tied somebody down to a bench and cut him up. Is he a nice guy or a mean guy? That is not enough information. The action itself is not a sure sign, and to think that any person who does that action necessarily means this is incorrect.

That leads to a lot of people making judgments about people, and a lot of unnecessary hatred. A person knows what that action would mean if somebody were coming from where he is coming from, with his background, his culture and his motives. But for this person, unless you know enough about him to see where he is coming from, you have to get a bigger picture before you can judge what the action means for him. It is just like a word: even if you know its definition, without its context and the tone of voice it is said in, you will not necessarily know what it means. You have to see the big picture.

To the point that a person could do something the Torah says is a sin, and it could really be representing his desire to connect to G-d, if he was misled and told that this is a good thing. Say a *tinok shenishba* (a child taken captive, raised without Torah) was brought up being told that if you want to connect to G-d you should do this: then it is actually expressing a good thing, only he is expressing it the wrong way. In the same way a person can use a word incorrectly because he does not really know what it means, and from the context you can figure out what he really means.

That is the general idea of *gilui ha'helem*: something that is essentially not connected, once it becomes associated, reveals the essence. The essential bias, the fact that he will always look to *chesed*, is from the essence; the particular things he does are not. Therefore a person can do things that are outwardly *gevura'dik* (stern) because of a motivation of *chesed*.

In educating a child, a parent or a teacher very often has to be strict, which is outwardly the opposite of what they want to do. But as the Rebbe Rashab says in *Chinuch Lanaar*, if you consistently mean the child's best, the child will pick up on that, sense that you are doing it for his best, and respond positively. If you are not doing it for his best, he will notice that too, and he will not want to listen.

One of the main things there is if the child sees a double standard: he is told to do something, told that it is a good thing, and then the parents do not want to do it. The parent may mean well, but it will not have a great effect. Like they say, parents who tell their kids not to do what they did have kids who tell their kids not to do what they did. When guests come, parents may expect the kids to give up things for the guests. They could do it because they really think it is right, are willing to do it themselves and want to teach their kid; or because they do not want to discomfort themselves, so they make the kids do it. Then the kids will resent it. But if they see the parents doing it themselves, just trying to teach them to be kind, they will appreciate it and learn to be kind.

The next class reads it again: the will that is born revealed is only like the revealing of an appearance of the essence, **like the movement that shows that something's alive**. The movement is not the actual life. It is not that if you take something and make it move, it is alive, not at all. But if something is alive, it is going to move.

blocks.title: Is the baby blind or deaf?
blocks.text: And the revealing of life in a separate thing, the body: here **the *gilui hachayus* means the consciousness**. How do you know that a person has a conscious soul? Because his eyes follow you if you move in front of him: his eyes respond physically to a stimulus of sight. How do they know if a baby is blind or deaf? If you clap next to its ear and it does not respond at all; if water is poured over its eye and it does not shut it; if it does not flinch when something is waved in front of its face. From the physical responses you know whether it has a spiritual consciousness of those things.

**Since the soul is essentially alive**, **it reveals the fact that it's alive by moving the body.** **And since the soul essentially has a consciousness**, **it also has physical perception when it's in the body**, **which is called physical life.**

phrases.he: כי גלוי רצון זה בא בדבר נבדל, שהוא ענין זה של חסד או דין
אבל מקור המוליד רצון זה
הוא בא מכח עצם המדה לבד
phrases.en: it only comes from *etzem hamidda*

blocks.text: For the revealing of this will comes in a separate thing. It is the same as with the soul: that the soul, since it is alive, has these abilities is from the essence; the soul essentially possesses the ability to move things, to control things, to be conscious of things. But whether it will be revealed in the body or not is not essential. That is only revealing; it is not essentially connected. It is a symptom, not the actual essence. So too the will that comes out: **it only comes from *etzem hamidda*** (the essence of the attribute), but it is not actually *etzem hamidda*.

sections.title: One source, many wills: the born will is not what you really want
sections.summary: One essential attribute gives birth to a separate will for each situation, through the associations made in *Adam Kadmon*. The born will was never wanted for itself: take away its connection and it vanishes, which is why the world is *yesh me'ayin*, and why prayer must lead the animal soul back to what it really wants.

phrases.he: ומובן ממילא, בהיות שיש כמה אופני דברים שיוליד רצון מיוחד לכל אחד ממקור אחד,
phrases.en: And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*.

phrases.he: שהוא תלוי בעצם המדה תמיד כו'
וגם שכל המטה תמיד כלפי רצון וחסד, היינו רק מצד עצם מדת החסד
phrases.en: the fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature

phrases.he: שמוליד תמיד רצון ושכל לחסד דוקא
ויש כמה ענינים נבדלים
phrases.en: but there are many different things that this will be expressed,

phrases.he: ולכל אחד מוליד רצון ושכל בפני עצמו כו'
phrases.en: and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.

phrases.he: ודי למבין

blocks.text: **And so it's understood that in many different *retzonos*, each one will have its own *ratzon*, but they're all coming from one *makor*** (source), which always depends on the essence of the attribute. A person who is essentially nice will want many different things in order to express that essential *midda* (attribute), and it will come out in different ways according to the situation. Sometimes it can come out in a way you would normally associate with *gevura* (might, restraint), like a surgeon.

And an intellect that always leans towards will and kindness is only from the essence of the attribute of kindness. **The fact that a person is always biased towards *chesed* is because they have an essential kind nature.** So this is a sign: the fact that he always has particular wills for *chesed* shows that he has an essential *midda* of *chesed*. **But there are many different things that this will be expressed**, **and this essential *midda* will create an individual *ratzon* for each scenario.**

So this is what *Adam Kadmon* does: it makes the connection between the essential *middos*, which are the *igulim* of *Adam Kadmon*, and the particular wills, the wills of *Atzilus*. The wills of *Atzilus* are not the essential will. A will to cut somebody is a particular will, and you do not know whether it is a will of *chesed* or of *din* (judgement) unless you see how it is associated. The association of what this will accomplish is made in *Adam Kadmon*. A person makes a self-image and a worldview, an association of what will accomplish what, so that he knows: in this situation my essential desire for *chesed* will be expressed like this, and my desire for *gevura* like that. The connection between the two is made in *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.title: Hunger becomes a desire to eat
blocks.text: The same on a physical level. Because of the body's makeup, the soul's desire to express itself freely in the body becomes associated with the desire to eat and drink and all these things: once it is enclothed in the body, those inner desires become associated with other desires. And the next step down, the desire to get rid of the pain in the stomach when a person is hungry becomes a desire to eat. Why? Because you learn that eating takes away that pain and gives you strength, so if you feel weak or hungry, right away a desire for food is created. It is not the essential desire, it is a created thing; but once they are associated, the one reveals the other. That is the idea of *gilui ha'helem*.

phrases.he: ומובן על כל פנים שיש הפרש גדול בין גלוי הרצון לחסד, שאינו רק בחינת גלוי ההעלם של עצם הרצון, המוליד רצון זה
phrases.en: So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon*.

phrases.he: שהוא בא מכח עצם המדה, שהוא אינו בחינת נבדל כו' ודי למבין.

blocks.text: **So from this we understand there's a big difference between the *ratzon* that's born out as a *gilui* from the *etzem ratzon* and the *etzem ratzon***, which comes from the power of the essence of the attribute and is not a separate thing. The will that comes out is detached from your essence: you do not really want it. The essential will you really want.

blocks.title: I never wanted to drive
blocks.text: A guy is hungry. He has a whole plan: he is going to get pizza, he wants to get in his car and drive, he gets his shoes on. A guy walks into the room and says, "Look, I brought pizza." So he starts taking his shoes back off. The other guy says, "I thought you wanted to drive to the store and everything." "No, no, I never wanted it at all."

That is the meaning of the world being created *yesh me'ayin* (something from nothing): the external things of the world are not really what G-d wants at all. You would not have to do anything to get him not to want to drive down the block; he never really wanted it in the first place. He wanted it only because it was connected to something he did want, and if that connection were taken away, the desire for it would vanish at once. You do not have to do anything, because it never really had its own *metzius* (existence).

And that itself is the point of *davenen* (praying): first to take your *nefesh habehamis* (animal soul) and show it that what it really wants requires that it connect to G-d. That is what it really wants, if it goes back to find its essential desire. Most people are not conscious of this. That is the problem: if you ask a person what he wants, he associates a certain form with what he wants and becomes stuck in it. If it does not work out the way he wanted he is disappointed, and he forgets that it was not really what he wanted.

This can happen because a person really can choose to want whatever he wants. He could decide to make something that is normally a *prat* (a detail) his essential goal. It is not his inner essence, but he has *bechira* (free choice). Once he has a *kavana* (intention), he makes a hierarchy of his inner will and his external will and everything.

With people, any time they have these kinds of problems, you always have to do both: there is the *naaseh* side and the *nishma* side ("we will do" and "we will understand"). Starting from scratch and having people refine their view of what they want is an *is'hapcha* thing (transforming the feeling itself): it will actually change their desire. That is the real meaning of *moach shalit al halev*, the mind rules the heart: when you change the way you look at things, or what you associate a thing with, it automatically changes the way you feel about it. Your feeling is a born will that comes out from your essential will through your *sechel*, which is what creates these associations; change that, and it automatically does an *is'hapcha*.

But until a person can do that, he has to start with *iskafya* (forcing oneself against the feeling). And there is a *maala* (an advantage) in it too; that is the idea of *Pada b'shalom nafshi mikrav li*. If the whole thing were that a person should realize the truth, be inspired and be a *tzaddik* (righteous man), *Hashem* could have made us *tzaddikim*. But *Hashem* also wants us to have *avoda* (divine service), to work. So He made it that there is always a level we enjoy and a level we do not; no matter what level you reach, there is always an *iskafya* you can do, you can always push yourself to do more and work harder. The whole reason *Hashem* made you not feel like doing things is to give you the opportunity for a meaningful relationship: when you make yourself sit and do something you do not feel like doing in order to connect to G-d, that is meaningful, because you are actually giving something up.

That is the *naaseh*, the first thing, and it is really a prerequisite: the willingness to push a little is what gives him the ability to have the *nishma* afterwards. So first he has to make *hachlatos* (resolutions) to do things, just externally: all the things of *halacha* you are supposed to do, to make sure the place is nice, to stand nicely, to look in the *Siddur*, not to talk during *davenen*, not to take his *tefillin* off early. If you do things to try to get out early, that will mess it up. So first you have to get the *naaseh* right: to make an effort, even if you do not feel like it, like finishing *Tehillim* before you take your *tefillin* off, whatever it is for you, to show that you are making this a priority. Once you do that, you have to start to understand and appreciate what is going on when you are *davenen*.

sections.title: Atzilus called out from Adam Kadmon: lights, Moshe's spirit, the Kesarim
sections.summary: The ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are only what was hidden in *Adam Kadmon* coming out, so they are called lights, like the spirit drawn off Moshe onto the elders without his losing any. Their *Kesarim* are revealed wills, like the will to give a poor man a dollar, which *Adam Kadmon* ties to the essential will.

phrases.he: ועל דרך משל זה יובן ענין קורא הדורות מראש דאדם קדמון כו'
כמשל הקורא דבר שיצא מהעלמו לגלוי לחוץ
כך כל עיקר בחינת עשר ספירות דאצילות הוא שיצאו מהעלמם לגלוי בלבד
phrases.en: the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui*.

phrases.he: ועל כן נקראו בשם אורות או ספירות,
phrases.en: That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros*,

phrases.he: כמו זיו ואור

blocks.text: By this *mashal* we can understand *kore hadoros meirosh* of *Adam Kadmon*: like calling out a thing so that it comes out of its hiding into the open, as if there were a guy hiding behind a curtain and you said, "Okay, come out now." So **the whole *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* is that they were *b'helem* in *Adam Kadmon*, and now they're just coming out *b'gilui***.

Once *Hashem* had the essential wills for the *dira b'tachtonim* (a dwelling below), which is the *igul* of *Adam Kadmon*, He created in *Adam Kadmon* the general image of what will fulfil those wills. Then, automatically, when a particular situation comes up in the world, G-d knows the particular will: the Torah and *mitzvos*, how *Hashem* wants you to act in this situation, is a *gilui* that comes *mimeila* (by itself) from *Adam Kadmon*. *Adam Kadmon* already made the associations, the connection of this thing to the essential will, and the situation just reveals what was already decided in *Adam Kadmon*.

**That's why what comes out in *Atzilus* is called *oros*, or *sefiros***, like radiance and light. It is only a revelation of the *etzem*: *Adam Kadmon* is like the *Maor*, the *etzem*, and the revelations that come in *Atzilus* are only a revelation. *Atzilus* is that *Hashem* is going to reveal Himself as creating a world.

Say the *chesed* of *Arich* is the light of the *chesed* of *Atzilus*. The *chesed* of *Arich* is that anything *Hashem* creates is constantly, every moment, recreated by Him, because He is the true *metzius* and anything that exists depends on Him. The fact that a created thing has to be recreated every single second is a *gilui* of the essential thing, that *Hashem* is the true *metzius*, which is like *Adam Kadmon*. *Hashem* decided in *Adam Kadmon* to reveal Himself as a creator, and not just a creator but the ultimate creator: that means He is essentially a creator.

What does it mean to be essentially a creator? That anything that exists is totally dependent on Him. The fact that our world is created by Him every single moment is a *gilui* of that essential thing. It is not the actual G-dliness; it is like a symptom. If you see a world being created every single moment, that tells you what its relationship to its Creator is like, and so it tells you something about the Creator.

phrases.he: וכמו כל בחינת גלוי ההעלם שאינו רק בבחינת אור, וכבחינת מראה וגוון,
וכמו תנועת החי כו'
phrases.en: like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive.

phrases.he: והיינו כמו ויאצל מן הרוח,
phrases.en: this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*.

phrases.he: שאין זה רוחו של משה
phrases.en: this is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach*,

phrases.he: רק בחינת גלוי אורו וזיוו לבד, הוא שנאצל והופרש, כגלוי שלהבת מן הגחלת וכהאי גוונא כו'

blocks.text: As every revealing of the hidden is only like light, like an appearance and color, and like the movement of a living thing: **like the movement of a living thing reveals that it's alive**. And that is why it is called *Atzilus*, from *vayatzel min haruach*: **this is like it says by Moshe, that *Hashem* took some of Moshe's spirit and put it on the seventy *zekeinim*** (elders). **This is not Moshe's actual *ruach*, it's not like he lost his *ruach***; only the revealing of his light and radiance was drawn off and set apart, like the revealing of a flame from the coal. As it says in Rashi, it is like a candle from which you can light many other candles, and the original candle does not lose any of its flame. It is not *etzem v'hispashtus*; Moshe did not give up some of his *ruach*.

blocks.title: The Rebbe's shluchim
blocks.text: When the Rebbe sends out *shluchim* (emissaries), the *shluchim* have a little of the Rebbe's *ruach* in them: they go with the Rebbe's ideology. The more they make themselves *batel* (nullified) to the Rebbe's will, the more successful they will be, because the Rebbe knows what he is doing, sees things a lot better than we do, and knows the actual reality of the way things work, what everything is for, why things are the way they are and what is supposed to be going on. You do not actually have to become Moshe. As long as you are able to nullify yourself to his will, you will reveal his *ruach*.

blocks.title: A conduit for G-d's wisdom
blocks.text: The same with a person who learns Torah. It is really G-d's wisdom, not his. But if he works to understand it, to make himself just understand what G-d is saying, people will think he is very smart. It is not his own thing; he just became a better conduit for it.

So too *Hashem* made the elders conduits to Moshe's *ruach*: He opened them up to see better, with a little of Moshe's *ruach hakodesh* (holy spirit), his *nevua* (prophecy), so that they were able to know the truth for being judges.

phrases.he: וכל זה יובן על פי משל הנזכר לעיל מענין גלוי הרצון בדבר נבדל
phrases.en: So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*,

phrases.he: שיוצא מהעלם עצם הרצון שמצד עצמיות כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character.

phrases.he: כך בחינת כתרים דעשר ספירות דאצילות הן רק בחינת גלוי רצון לגבי העלם עצם הרצון שנקרא רצון לרצון,
שהוא בבחינת אדם קדמון כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: **So this is all like the *mashal* of the *gilui ratzon*** in a separate thing, **which comes out from the *etzem haratzon*, which is that a person's essential bias comes from his essential character**. So the *Kesarim* (the crowns) of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* are only a revealed will, compared with the hidden essential will called *ratzon l'ratzon* (a will for a will). The wills of *Atzilus* are a particular desire, a *gilui*, like the desire to give somebody a dollar. The will in *Adam Kadmon* is the *etzem*, the bias, the *ratzon l'ratzon*: the association that makes giving a poor person a dollar count as nice, and so ties the desire to give him a dollar to the essential will for *chesed*. And that connects it to the essential will, the *ratzon kadum* (the preceding will) before *Adam Kadmon*, the *igulim* before *Adam Kadmon*.

So if a person wants *chesed*, then because *Adam Kadmon* tells him that this is connected, he will want this. The same way, since *Hashem* decided He wanted a *dira b'tachtonim* in a certain order, that makes the Torah. The *chachma* (wisdom) of the Torah is to be *batel* to *Adam Kadmon*: to tell you accurately, in each situation, what will get you closer to the *dira b'tachtonim* and what will get you farther away. That is the teaching of the Torah.

If *Hashem* would decide that He wants the *dira* in a different way, the revealed will would automatically change too. There are certain things *Hashem* said will not change, and that is why they cannot. But essentially, it is not that putting on *tefillin* is good and not putting them on is bad. *Hashem* decided that He wants it, so now it is connected to G-d, and so now it is good.

phrases.he: וכמו מבחינת העלם הרצון דחסד דאדם קדמון נמשך גלוי רצון לחסד דאצילות שנקרא כתר דחסד כו'
וכן מבחינת העלם רצון דחכמה כו'
phrases.en: from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: As from the hidden will for *chesed* of *Adam Kadmon* is drawn the revealed will for *chesed* of *Atzilus*, called the *Keser* of *chesed*. The fact that *Hashem* decided to reveal Himself as a creator became a will to create our world. Our world is only one example: creating it is not the essential thing, that *Hashem* is a creator. We just see that *Hashem* created this world. But since He is always creating it, every moment, all the time, that reveals the *etzem* to us: we see that He is a creator.

And so from the hidden will for *chachma*: **from the *etzem ratzon* of *chachma* comes the *chachma* of *Atzilus***. Since *Hashem* wanted to reveal Himself as wise, He had a will in *Atzilus* to have wisdom in the world and in the Torah. And so when we look around the world, we see a lot of wisdom in it.

sections.title: From Malchus of Adam Kadmon to the Keser of Atzilus: the giver's speech becomes the receiver's will
sections.summary: Only the outer expression, the *Malchus*, of each level becomes the *Keser* of the next: a person's self-image measures each situation, the king's spoken wish becomes the servant's own will, and the teacher's words become the student's understanding. So the external letters of *Adam Kadmon* define *Atik* and *Arich*, and all of history is chosen from what is in *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: אך כמו שמובן ממשל הנזכר לעיל שזהו הנקרא התהוות רצון לרצון,
הרי הוא בא בבחינת הכלל
phrases.en: so it's like a *klal*,

phrases.he: להוליד כמה מיני רצון וכמה ענינים אופנים שונים כו',
phrases.en: and includes many particular things: whatever each circumstance, that inner *etzem ratzon* to be kind will come out in different ways.

phrases.he: כך מבחינת רצון לרצון לחסד באדם קדמון נולד כמה מיני גלוי רצון של חסד באצילות
phrases.en: So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.

blocks.text: But as is understood from the *mashal*, this is called the coming into being of a *ratzon l'ratzon*. *Adam Kadmon* is like the general will for everything that you are ever going to do, **so it's like a *klal*** (a general whole), **and includes many particular things: whatever each circumstance, that inner *etzem ratzon* to be kind will come out in different ways**. **So too, the *etzem ratzon* for *chesed* comes out in many different particular *inyanim* in *Atzilus*.**

phrases.he: והענין הוא דמבחינת המלכות של מדה דאדם קדמון נעשה בחינת כתר דמדה דאצילות
phrases.en: from the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: ובכללות העשר ספירות הרי רק מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר דאצילות
והוא רק מבחינת אותיות וגלוי עצם העלם הרצון, נעשה אור העצם של גלוי רצון כו'
(שהוא כמו שמבואר באות הי''ח
דרק מבחינת סוף מעשה דעצם הרצון נעשה רצון לרצון שהוא עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון)
phrases.en: only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*,

blocks.title: The self-image of a talmid chacham
blocks.text: The matter is that **from the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus***. The *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is the external form, a definable thing. Say a person creates a self-image and knows clearly what he wants: it is as if it whispers in his ear that he wants to be, say, a *talmid chacham* (a Torah scholar). It always tells him that he wants to be that. And the external thing, the *Malchus* of it, is that he has a whole picture, a whole *hanhaga* (conduct), of what it means to be a guy like that. Whenever he comes to a situation, he looks at that external form he pictures himself in, and measures: "Well, does this fit with this form?" If it fits, he has a will for it; if it does not, he has a will against it. That is what creates the *Keser* of his particular things, which is like the *Keser* of *Atzilus*.

It is only from the letters and the revealing of the hidden essential will that the essential light of the revealed will comes into being, as was explained in section 18: only from the last level of the deed of the essential will comes the *ratzon l'ratzon*, the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*. Just as **only from *Malchus* of the *igulim* becomes *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon***, so too only from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* comes *Keser* of *Atzilus*. Now he is going to give us a *mashal* for this.

phrases.he: (על דרך דוגמא, מגלוי רצון שבדבור המשפיע נעשה עצם הרצון למקבל
כמו שמאותיות גלוי השכל שבדבור שבמשפיע נעשה עצם אור השכל במקבל
phrases.en: How the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher.

phrases.he: וכך רק מאותיות וגלוי חסד שבדבור דמשפיע נעשה אור הרצון לחסד למקבל
כידוע בכל עילה ועלול,
phrases.en: this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul*,

phrases.he: שמבחינת האחרונה שבעילה נעשה ראש ושרש לעלול
phrases.en: That his *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*.

blocks.title: Your wish is my command
blocks.text: By way of example: from the will revealed in the speech of the *mashpia* (the giver) comes the essential will of the *mekabel* (the receiver). Take a servant. The servant tells the king, "Your wish is my command." The servant's will is really for the *baal haratzon*, the one whose will it is: he really wants to do what the king says. So how does he know what to want? Whatever the king tells him, the external revealing of the king's will, becomes his will.

That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): when you give over the point of your will and dedicate yourself, anything he tells you to do automatically becomes your full inner will, and you have *mesirus nefesh* for it. This particular thing he told you to do is not the essential will, but since it is connected, since he said to do it, it now gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*. If a person tried to stop you, you would die or kill him or whatever, so as not to let him stop you.

sensitivity.reason: Says that with mesirus nefesh a servant would kill a person who tried to stop him carrying out the order; out of context it reads as approving violence.
sensitivity.publishable: That is *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice): when you give over the point of your will and dedicate yourself, anything he tells you to do automatically becomes your full inner will, and you have *mesirus nefesh* for it. This particular thing he told you to do is not the essential will, but since it is connected, since he said to do it, it now gets the full force of your *mesirus nefesh*. Nothing anyone did could stop you.

blocks.title: The student and the teacher
blocks.text: The same with a teacher: the student's inner knowledge comes from the words of the intellect. As from the letters of the intellect revealed in the giver's speech comes the essential light of the receiver's intellect: **how the students get their *sechel* from the letters of the teacher**. The students have an essential thing, that they want to learn whatever this guy knows. They have a general dedication: they believe he is an expert who has something they do not know, and therefore, whatever he says, they accept as true.

To really learn properly, you have to be *batel* and accept, even if you do not understand: accept that he knows better than you, and just try to understand what he is saying. If you are going to accept that maybe what he said is not true, then you might not understand it properly; since you do not understand it properly it will not make sense, and then you will say it is not true. But if you know that this guy knows it, you will just try to understand what he is saying, and that is what will guarantee that you understand it properly.

And so only from the letters and the revealing of kindness in the giver's speech comes the light of the will for kindness in the receiver. There are different things like this. If a person loves somebody, and that person says good things about somebody else, he will also love that one, because he trusts him. It can also go the other way: even for oneself, saying good things about somebody wakes up love for him in oneself. But here he means saying good things about somebody to someone else, which makes him feel love for that person. As is known, **this is the way it works in every *ila v'alul***: the last level of the cause becomes the head and root of the effect. **His *chitzoniyus* becomes your *pnimiyus*** (his outside becomes your inside).

phrases.he: וכך מבחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון בכלל נעשה בחינת כתר דעתיק יומין כו'
phrases.en: the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*.

phrases.he: דהיינו מבחינת גלוי רצון לרצון שבדבור בלבד,
נעשה בחינת מקור כל גלוי רצון שמצד התענוג שנקרא כתר דעתיק יומין כו' וכמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: And so from *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* in general comes the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*: **the whole thing of *Atik* and *Arich* is defined based on the external *osios* of *Adam Kadmon*** (its letters). That is, from the revealing of the *ratzon l'ratzon* in speech alone: *Hashem* chooses which part of the *ratzon l'ratzon* is going to come out now. That is *kore hadoros meirosh*: He picks which generation is going to come out now, and which one He picks to reveal makes the way all the wills come out.

It becomes the source of every revealed will that comes from the *taanug* (delight), called the *Keser* of *Atik Yomin*, as will be explained. In a person, the whole inner delight, the fact that he enjoys something, depends on his seeing it as fulfilling his self-image, and therefore he will enjoy it. If he sees it as against his self-image, he will hate it; he will not enjoy it. We will learn later what *ratzon* and *taanug* are, but it is the same way with G-d.

phrases.he: והיינו כללות ענין העשר ספירות דאצילות שיצאו מהעלם עשר ספירות דאדם קדמון, כמו שכתוב קורא הדורות מראש כו':
phrases.en: That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: And this is the whole matter of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, which came out of the concealment of the ten *sefiros* of *Adam Kadmon*, as it says, *kore hadoros meirosh*. **That's the *inyan* of the *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, that they are only a *gilui* of the *etzem* thing of *Adam Kadmon*.** *Adam Kadmon* is that *Hashem* chose the essential form in which He wants to reveal Himself in this world, which is the ten *sefiros* in general, a certain form of those things.

It is also the form of *Moshiach* and of the *dira b'tachtonim* that *Hashem* chose. Based on that, *Hashem* chooses how to conduct the world all the time, depending on which aspect of *Adam Kadmon* He is revealing now; the way the world is going to go, the whole of history, is really defined by it. That is why *nevua* is possible: if you know what the story is in *Adam Kadmon*, you know how it is going to come out down the line.

reviewQuestions.question: What is the difference between *etzem v'hispashtus* and *gilui ha'helem*, and how do the sunlight in a room and the sun seen through the window show both?
Why are movement, speech and the color of an apple truer *meshalim* for *gilui ha'helem* than the flame hidden in a coal?
How do you know that a person is kind or cruel, and why can a single act, like tying a man to a bench and cutting him, not tell you?
What does the man who takes his shoes back off when the pizza arrives show about the born will, and what does it teach about the world and about *davenen*?
Why are the *sefiros* of *Atzilus* called lights, and what does Moshe's spirit placed on the seventy elders show about them?
How does the servant who says "Your wish is my command" explain that only the *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* becomes the *Keser* of *Atzilus*?
